archetype.name: Playoff Team (two-star offense, leaky edges)
archetype.definition: A Denver side whose Jokić-Murray core and five-year track record say it belongs in the playoff field, but whose first five games have looked more like a middling team than a contender.

report.headline: 3-2 hides a middling start: elite guards and center, nothing on the wing.
report.take:
Denver opens 2026-27 at 3-2, but the margin tells a plainer story than the record. The Nuggets have been outscored by 6 over five games, a Net Rtg of -1.2 that ranks 19th, and the point differential implies two wins, not three. Two of those games were lopsided losses: 84-96 at Oklahoma City and 114-134 at home to Golden State. One of the wins took overtime against New Orleans. This is a team that has made a habit of being good. It won 54, 50, 57 and 53 games the last four seasons and led the league in offensive rating a year ago. So the real question is how much of this start is the real team.

The engine is where it always is. Jamal Murray has been the best player on the floor: 129 points on a 64.4 TS %, with the team 25.9 points per 100 better when he plays. Nikola Jokić is filling every column, with 49 rebounds and 46 assists, even if his 55.4 TS % is ordinary by his standards. That pairing earns the A+ backcourt and A- frontcourt grades. The problem is everything between them. The wings grade is D-. DeMar DeRozan has a 50.7 TS %, a -6.2 BPM and a -19.1 On-Off in the most wing minutes. Bryce Hopkins sits at -10.2 BPM behind him. Opposing small forwards are piling up the most points, rebounds and assists of any position against this defense, ranked 30th in the league.

The offense hasn't fallen apart, but it has slipped from historic to merely good. The ORtg is 114.6 (11th) against 122.6 last season, and most of that drop is ball security. The TOV % has jumped to 14.7 (21st) from 11.5 a year ago. The shooting is still there, with a 37.4 3P % ranked 7th, and turnovers are the most fixable kind of slippage. The defense ranks 21st, which matches last season, so it isn't news. What is new is how porous the paint has been. Opponents take 34.4% of their shots at the rim, 28th in the league, and Denver is grabbing only 70.5% of available defensive rebounds.

Where this goes depends on how you weigh five games against five seasons. The talent at the top and the history argue for a rebound toward the high-40s or 50s. The pace numbers of 49 wins and a -98 differential capture the tension: the record projects like a playoff team, the margin doesn't. Until the wing minutes produce something, Denver is a very good two-man team with a soft middle, and this week's schedule will test that hard.

strengths.title: Murray and Jokić carry everything
strengths.body: Murray is scoring efficiently, and Denver's net rating swings sharply in his favor when he plays. Jokić is the league's best facilitating big again, with assists nearly matching his rebounds. Both are top-five at their positions on the site. That core has driven five straight winning seasons, so this is the part of the start most likely to hold.

strengths.title: Shot-making still travels
strengths.body: Denver is making 37.4% of its threes, 7th in the league and well above the league's 34.7. It is also getting to the line more than average, so the eFG % and TS % both sit in the top third. The volume from three is low, but the conversion matches what this group shot last season, so it looks like a real skill rather than a hot week.

concerns.title: The wing hole is enormous
concerns.body: The wings grade is D-. DeRozan's minutes have been a net loss: a 50.7 TS %, a -6.2 BPM and a -19.1 On-Off. The backups haven't helped either. Defensively, opposing small forwards rank dead last in combined points, rebounds and assists allowed. Without a better answer from the roster, this is a structural weakness, not a slump.

concerns.title: Turnovers have dulled the offense
concerns.body: Last season's league-best offense took care of the ball, with an 11.5 TOV %. This year it is 14.7, ranked 21st, and the ORtg has fallen from 122.6 to 114.6. Turnover rate is noisy over five games, so this should drift back toward the team's norm. Still, it is the main reason the offense ranks 11th instead of near the top.

concerns.title: Paint and glass leaking on defense
concerns.body: Opponents are getting to the rim at one of the highest rates in the league, and finishing there above league average. Denver's 70.5 DRB % ranks 23rd, well below its usual mid-70s. A 21st-ranked defense was already true last season, so the floor is familiar. The rebounding slide is the new piece to watch.

trend.note: Denver has alternated a loss and a win through its first five games, including two double-digit defeats and an overtime escape, before closing October with road wins at New Orleans and Phoenix. Too few games to call a direction beyond up-and-down.

weekAhead.headline: Three top-11 teams in four games, two of them elite
weekAhead.body:
This is a demanding week. Portland (4-1, 2nd on the site, +11.4 Net Rtg) and Toronto (3-3 but a +7.6 Net Rtg) come to Denver before a road trip to Indiana and Houston (6-1, the league's top offense). Portland's defense keeps opponents away from the rim better than almost anyone. Toronto forces turnovers at the league's highest rate, and that is exactly where Denver has been sloppiest. Houston pairs the best ORtg in the league with elite offensive rebounding, aimed squarely at Denver's weak defensive glass.

The soft spot is Indiana, 2-5 with a defense ranked 22nd. It gives up a lot to centers and the second-most points to small forwards of any team, which sets up a big Jokić night. A 2-2 week would be a fair result. Losing the home games to Portland and Toronto would put the margin problem into the record.

keyMatchups.title: Ball security against Toronto's pressure
keyMatchups.body: Toronto's defense forces turnovers more often than any in the league. Denver is turning it over at a bottom-third rate. If the Nuggets' carelessness is real, this is the game that exposes it.

keyMatchups.title: Jokić against Portland's soft middle
keyMatchups.body: Portland is elite almost everywhere but has given up 24 points a game to centers, near the bottom of the league. Its defense is built to wall off the rim and smother point guards, so the offense should run through Jokić rather than Murray.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's offensive glass
keyMatchups.body: Houston grabs its own misses at the 3rd-best rate in the league and has the No. 1 ORtg. Denver's defensive rebounding ranks 23rd. Second chances could decide the road finale.

weekAhead.watch: Whether anyone on the wing can hold up against Portland's A- wings and Houston's B+ group, or whether opposing small forwards keep feasting.

restOfSeason.body: The core is proven and the shooting is real, so expect the offense to climb back toward the top tier as the turnover rate normalizes. The defense should settle around where it has lived for two seasons: below average, but not a disaster. The wing production is the piece that won't fix itself. Unless DeRozan's efficiency recovers, Denver will lean on Murray and Jokić more than a contender should. That points to a playoff team in the high-40s to low-50s rather than the top seed its talent at the top suggests. The overtime win means a little record luck is baked in, so the margin needs to catch up for the record to hold.
swingFactors: Turnover rate returning toward last season's
Wing production from DeRozan and the bench

confidence.note: Five games; the team's history weighs more than the margin so far.
